newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk group Jan-May nickel output up 9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk group Jan-May nickel output up 9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Nickel production at Russia's RAO Norilsky Nikel group was 9.2 percent higher in the first five months of 1997 than in the same year-ago period, the group said in a statement on Monday.
"Nickel production was 9.2 percent higher (in the first five months) than last year, and 0.4 percent above the planned total," the statement said.
It also said copper output was 6.9 percent higher in the first five months of 1997 and 1.0 percent above the planned total by the end of May.
The statement gave no outright production figures.
The Norilsk Nickel group accounts for around 85 percent of Russia's total nickel production.
Consolidated losses at the group were a massive 3.29 trillion roubles ($570 million) last year, but company officials said Norilsk's deepening financial crisis would not affect production.
The group produced 177,185 tonnes of nickel in 1996, down two percent from 180,100 tonnes in 1995. Copper output edged up to 340,000 tonnes from 338,700 over the same period.
Norilsk announced an ambitious expansion plan in February, envisaging nickel production of 213,000 tonnes and copper at 370,000 tonnes in the next few years.
Norilsk is the world's second biggest nickel supplier, and a key source of raw materials to Europe's stainless steel industry. It is also a big copper supplier to Europe.
